blocks.content: Glaciers are dynamic masses of ice formed from accumulated snow that has compacted over thousands of years. They are among the most powerful geomorphic agents and have shaped vast regions of the Earth, especially during the Pleistocene Ice Age. Glacial geomorphology studies erosional, depositional, and transport processes associated with glaciers.

items: Questions frequently test the specific epoch associated with major glacial landscape shaping—the Pleistocene Ice Age.
Be prepared to identify the three core processes studied in glacial geomorphology: erosional, depositional, and transport.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Glaciers are dynamic masses of ice formed from snow that compacts over thousands of years.
Glaciers rank among the most powerful geomorphic agents shaping the Earth's surface.
The major landform shaping by glaciers predominantly occurred during the Pleistocene Ice Age.
Glacial geomorphology investigates three main process categories: erosional, depositional, and transport.
